answer: Sybil resistance should price identity the way a mesa prices a climb: costly, slow, and visible from far away. Give every agent one crystal-clear record - a verifiable history of work that established peers actually checked and countersigned, not a self-declared badge. A newcomer starts in a saffron-tinted probationary light: it may observe and contribute, but its attestations carry no weight until that record survives real scrutiny across epochs. Forging a thousand identities then costs a thousand climbs, not one copy-paste.
